foot_note: Summaries and facts verified against repo READMEs and GitHub APIs (2026-09-09)
insight: **The Agent Skill ecosystem dominates the charts**: Nearly two-thirds of the 24 trending spots are skill and agent framework projects. Even unconventional, niche-positioned projects like i-have-adhd (ADHD-friendly output) and ponytail ("the laziest staff engineer" / YAGNI) are pulling in thousands of stars within a single day or week.

**Tech giants and elite universities enter the fray**: OpenAI (official Codex plugin examples), Tencent (teamai-cli), Nous Research (hermes-agent), Tsinghua THU-MAIC (OpenMAIC), and Rails creator DHH (Omarchy) all made appearances across this period's top trending lists—building infrastructure for AI coding agents has become the ultimate battleground.

**Moving past Mermaid for architecture diagrams?** Both archify (#1 on the monthly chart, +44.2k stars) and diagram-design (+30.8k) lead with the pitch of "no more junk Mermaid diagrams," making self-contained HTML/SVG, verifiability, and reviewability the new key selling points for diagramming tools.

**The resurgence of personal productivity tools**: OpenLogi (a Rust-based Logitech replacement) and vorssaint-utils (an all-in-one macOS menu bar suite) both landed on the monthly charts. The local-first, telemetry-free niche of "open-source alternatives to paid utilities" is currently rivaling AI infrastructure in popularity.

rows.intro: A skill pack for AI coding assistants: forces them to put answers first—lead with action, use numbered steps, and eliminate fluff—delivering an output style optimized for users with ADHD (and better for everyone).
facts: Installs as a skill/plugin into CLI coding assistants like Claude Code (`INSTALL.md` instructions included); official docs state no ADHD diagnosis is required to benefit
Core rules: Action first + numbered steps; README includes before-and-after examples demonstrating how to avoid burying conclusions in lengthy explanations
README provided in 7 languages (EN, ZH, JA, PT, VI, KO, TH); MIT licensed; created in 2026-05
33k+ stars verified via GitHub API (as of 2026-09-09)

rows.intro: An editorial-grade diagramming skill for coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Pi: outputs self-contained HTML+SVG across 38+ diagram types—no low-effort Mermaid outputs, no decorative shadows.
facts: Officially covers 38/39 diagram types: Sankey, Fishbone, Wardley maps, Kanban, User Journeys, Deployment diagrams, Dependency graphs, UML Class diagrams, DB schemas, etc. (README v2.5.10 release notes)
Decouples semantic patterns from layout: queues, strategy tracking, and trust boundaries reuse existing base types to avoid infinite type bloat
Parses draw.io and Mermaid source files to redraw them at specified formats, dimensions, and detail levels; defaults to static HTML with optional accessible animations
MIT licensed; created in 2026-04 with a live preview site; 36k+ stars verified via GitHub API

rows.intro: A software development methodology of composable skills and guided instructions for coding agents: shifts agents from blindly writing code to a structured workflow that clarifies intent, confirms specs in chunks, and generates an actionable plan first.
facts: Core workflow: agent asks 'what are you actually trying to do?' → breaks specs into manageable chunks for confirmation → produces a clear implementation plan before coding (README 'How it works')
Supports 10+ agents including Claude Code, Codex CLI/App, Cursor, Devin CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok Build, Kimi Code, OpenCode, Pi, and Hermes Agent (README install directory)
Includes composable skills like `brainstorming`, `writing-plans`, and `subagent-driven-development`; tagged with `sdlc` and `skills`
MIT licensed; created in 2025-10; 280k+ stars verified via GitHub API
